title: Composition of quasi-finite ring maps
statement: Let $A\to B$ and $B\to C$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings. Assume that both maps are of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and quasi-finite at every prime of the target in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. Then the composite $A\to C$ is of finite type and quasi-finite at every prime of $C$.

mathlib_searches.query: composition of quasi-finite finite-type ring maps is quasi-finite at every prime
mathlib_searches.results: Hits include RingHom.QuasiFinite.comp (Mathlib/RingTheory/RingHom/QuasiFinite.lean:37) and stableUnderComposition (:55). Read RingHom.QuasiFinite (:24-25) and Algebra.QuasiFinite (Mathlib/RingTheory/QuasiFinite/Basic.lean:67-69): the predicate says each residue-field fibre is module-finite, and does not include finite type. The DAG uses finite type and isolated fibre primes.
mathlib_searches.verdict: candidate, not a one-line match: the equivalence between fibrewise module-finiteness and isolated-point quasi-finiteness under finite type is a separate bridge (delivery-errors B8)
